explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/698: 'Is there some h(n) → ∞ such that for all 2 <= i < j <= n/2, gcd(C(n,i), C(n,j)) >= h(n)?', resolved by Bergman [Be11] (gcd ≫ n^{1/2} 2^i / i^{3/2}). The statement asks for h : ℕ → ℕ tending to infinity with h(n) <= gcd(C(n,i), C(n,j)) for all n and all 2 <= i < j <= n/2 (natural division n/2 is floor, matching 'j <= n/2' for integers). This is exactly the question with a positive answer, as the `@[question]` convention prescribes for answered yes-questions. Faithful.
